subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The arms race intensified in 1957 when the USSR launched which milestone, alarming the West?
questions.explain: The launch of Sputnik in 1957 shocked the USA and intensified the space and arms race.

questions.q: The League of Nations failed to stop which 1931 act of aggression in the Far East?
options: The German remilitarisation of the Rhineland
questions.explain: The Japanese invasion of Manchuria in 1931 exposed the League's weakness.

questions.q: The Warsaw Pact, the Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern Bloc states, was created in which year?
questions.explain: The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955, partly in response to West Germany joining NATO.

questions.q: At which 1945 conference, held in February, did Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin agree that Germany would be divided into zones of occupation?
questions.explain: The Yalta Conference of February 1945 saw the Big Three agree to divide a defeated Germany into occupation zones.

questions.q: In which year did the United States announce the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan?
questions.explain: Both the Truman Doctrine and the Marshall Plan were announced in 1947 to contain the spread of communism.

questions.q: What was the total figure eventually set for German reparations after the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explain: Reparations were fixed at 6.6 billion pounds in 1921, a sum Germans deeply resented.

questions.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall, symbolising the end of the division of Europe?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall fell in November 1989 as the Eastern Bloc collapsed.

questions.q: After Munich, Hitler broke his promise by occupying the rest of which country in March 1939?
questions.explain: In March 1939 Hitler occupied the remainder of Czechoslovakia, ending British faith in appeasement.

questions.q: Which territory was taken from Germany and placed under League control for 15 years by the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explain: The Saar coalfield was placed under League administration for 15 years before a 1935 plebiscite.

questions.q: What was the Soviet response in 1949 to the Western Allies merging their zones to create West Germany and ending the airlift?
options: The signing of the Warsaw Pact
The creation of Comecon and the East German state
questions.explain: In 1949 the USSR set up the German Democratic Republic (East Germany), and Comecon coordinated Eastern Bloc economies.

questions.q: At the 1938 Munich Agreement, which territory was handed over to Germany?
questions.explain: The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler send troops to remilitarise the Rhineland in defiance of Versailles?
questions.explain: German troops remilitarised the Rhineland in 1936, with no Allied response.

questions.q: Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty, eliminating intermediate-range nuclear missiles, in which year?
questions.explain: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty was signed in 1987.

questions.q: In which year did Soviet tanks crush the Hungarian Uprising led by Imre Nagy?
questions.explain: The Hungarian Uprising of 1956 was suppressed when Soviet forces invaded Budapest.

questions.q: In which year did the USA and USSR sign the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (SALT I), a high point of detente?
questions.explain: SALT I was signed in 1972, limiting strategic nuclear weapons during the era of detente.

questions.q: The Cuban Missile Crisis, the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in October 1962 over Soviet missiles placed in Cuba.

questions.q: In which year did the USA drop atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, contributing to early Cold War tension?
questions.explain: The atomic bombs were dropped in August 1945, beginning the nuclear age that shaped the Cold War.

questions.q: Which 1946 speech by Winston Churchill in Fulton, Missouri popularised the phrase 'iron curtain'?
questions.explain: Churchill's 1946 Fulton speech warned that an 'iron curtain' had descended across Europe.

questions.q: In which year was the Soviet Union formally dissolved?
questions.explain: The USSR was formally dissolved in December 1991, ending the Cold War.

questions.q: In which year was the Berlin Wall first built, dividing the city overnight?
questions.explain: The Berlin Wall was constructed in 1961 to stop East Germans fleeing to the West.

questions.q: Which 1980 movement in Poland, led by Lech Walesa, challenged communist control through trade-union action?
questions.explain: Solidarity, founded in 1980 under Lech Walesa, became the first independent trade union in the Eastern Bloc.

questions.q: In which year did the Soviet Union invade Afghanistan, helping to end the era of detente?
questions.explain: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979 caused a sharp deterioration in superpower relations.
